title: Sudoku Board Check
statement:
Decide whether a partly filled 9x9 digit grid breaks the sudoku rules so far.

Contract
- `board` is a non-null 9x9 `char[][]`; each cell is a digit `'1'` to `'9'` or `'.'` for an empty cell.
- The board is valid when no digit repeats within any row, any column, or any of the nine 3x3 boxes that tile the grid. Empty cells never conflict with anything.
- Only the filled cells are judged: return `true` for a board that obeys the rules even if it could not be completed into a full solution.
- Do not mutate `board`.

Examples
- `isValid` on a grid whose filled cells never repeat in a row, column or box returns `true`.
- Two `4`s at the top-left corner box, one at row 0 column 0 and one at row 1 column 1, return `false`.
- Two `7`s in column 5, at rows 0 and 8, return `false`.

examples.input: board with filled cells only from a valid solved grid
'4' at (row 0, col 0) and (row 1, col 1), all else empty
'7' at (row 0, col 5) and (row 8, col 5), all else empty

hints: Three kinds of group must each hold at most one copy of every digit: rows, columns and boxes.
Keep a seen-set per row, per column and per box while scanning every cell once. The box of a cell is (row / 3) * 3 + col / 3.
Skip '.' cells and test all three sets before adding the digit. Intended complexity: O(1) time and O(1) space, because the board size is fixed at 81 cells (O(n) in the cell count n).
